```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r transform}
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr)
enroll <- read_csv("enrollment.csv")

enroll <- enroll |>
  mutate(gpa = na_if(gpa, 999))
```

```{r tests}
library(readr)
enroll <- read_csv("enrollment.csv")

cor.test(enroll$gpa, enroll$credits)
## The result shows a weak negative relationship with gpa and credits and the p value is not statistically significant.
t.test(gpa ~ graduated, data = enroll)
## The t-test p value is not statistically significant.
summary(aov(gpa ~ program, data = enroll))
## The F value and the p value show there is no statistical significance between the relationship of gpa and the multiple programs.
chisq.test(table(enroll$degree_level, enroll$graduated))
## The p value again shows no relationship between degree level and graduated.
summary(lm(gpa ~ credits, data = enroll))
## The p value shows no statistical significance between credits and gpa.
pp <- read_csv("pre_post_scores.csv")
t.test(pp$post, pp$pre, paired = TRUE)
## The p value is extremely small and shows a significant statistical difference between the pre and post scores.
```
